thread.title: Fitbit reports 3Q 2018 earnings results

author: Emily McCormick
title: Fitbit reports 3Q 2018 earnings results
text:
Fitbit ( FIT ) flexed.
The fitness electronics maker returned to profitability on a non-GAAP basis for the first time in two years and beat Wall Street’s expectations on the top and bottom lines.
Fitbit reported adjusted earnings of 4 cents per share, versus consensus estimates of a loss of a penny per share. Revenue came in at $394 million for the quarter, exceeding expectations of $381.2 million, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The company also gave full-year revenue guidance of $1.5 billion, slightly above average analyst expectations of $1.49 billion.
The San Francisco-based company sold 3.5 million devices in the third quarter, up from 2.7 million in the previous period. Average selling price increased 3% from the year-ago quarter to $108 per device, “driven by a growing mix of smartwatches,” the company said in a statement.
Shares of Fitbit spiked 10.67% to $5.22 each as of 4:15 p.m. ET Wednesday.
FILE- In this March 1, 2017, file photo, Fitbit’s new Alta HR device is displayed in New York. Fitbit Inc. reports financial results on Monday, Feb. 26, 2018. (AP Photo/Mark Lennihan, File) More Fitbit’s stock has taken a beating the past couple years as new entrants to the smartwatch and fitness tracking industry continue to cannibalize business. Fitbit’s share of the wearables markets fell 3.3 percentage points year-over-year to 9.5% in the second quarter, setting it behind Apple ( AAPL ) and Xiaomi ( 1810.HK ), according to a September report from market intelligence firm IDC .
Fitbit made a deliberate push into the medical technology space in the third quarter. In September, the company launched a new platform called Fitbit Care, which offers coaching to help users stick to fitness plans and manage chronic diseases, along with an app allowing users to pull their health data from a Fitbit or blood pressure monitor. Health insurer Humana in also announced in September it selected Fitbit Care as a preferred health coaching solution for its employer group segment, giving more than 5 million Humana members exposure to Fitbit’s services.
The announcements were well-received by analysts and earned Fitbit at least one upgrade. Michael Pachter of Wedbush Securities upgraded Fitbit to Outperform from Neutral earlier in October, citing Fitbit Care as a potential driver of device sales and recurring subscription revenue and calling Fitbit’s push into medical technology a “massive opportunity.”
Fitbit also announced the launch of one of its latest products, the Charge 3, during the third quarter in August. The fitness tracker hit shelves earlier in October, after the end of the third quarter.
Shares of Fitbit are down 17% this year as of market close Wednesday.
This post is developing.
—
